full_judgment: 8. The writ-petitioner was quite aware of, and participated in, the above mentioned inquiry process which is evident from his own statements made in paragraph No.  8 of the writ petition wherein the writ-petitioner categorically stated that he came to know about the cause of action on 2.10.2004, that is, two months before the cancellation of his allotment on 4.12.2004 and further allotment in the name of writ-respondent No. 7 on the same date (4.12.2004) and as such, in law there was no necessity for issuing any notice to the writ-petitioner For showing cause. Private properties of writ-respondent No. 7 i.e. H.S. plot No. 1435 (part) has been allotted in favour of the writ-petitioner and on coming to know about the said Fact he made an objection in writing to the concerned authority for cancelling the allotment of the writ-petitioner. Consequently, the writ-petitioner did not pay the remaining amount of the salami and no lease deed was executed in his favour. On 02.10.2004, the writ-petitioner submitted objection to respondent No. 1 informing him about the decision of cancellation of said allotment and re-allotment of the land in question in the name of writ-respondent No. 7. The writ-respondents considered the objection of the writ-petitioner by way of several physical investigations and as such, the writ-petition is not maintainable in the eye of law. Writ-respondent No. 7 Purchased 0.825 acre of land from R.S. plot Nos. 1435, 1436, 1437 of R.S. Khatian No. 496 corresponding to R.S. plots No. 3256 arid 3257 of R.S. Khatian No. 687 under mouza Gosaidanga Police Station Double mooring. District Chittagong vide registered deed No. 1849 dated 11.3.1999 and deed No. 2946 dated 6.5.1999. After purchase writ-respondent No. 7 mutated his time vide Mutation Case No.  6953 of 1998-99 dated 23.11.1999 and has been possessing the land. Here is a strip land of R.S. Plot No. 1101 adjacent to the land of R.S. plot No.  1.435. Writ-respondent No. 7 is the owner of R.S plot No.  1435; R.S. plot No. 1101 was acquired by the government and the writ-respondent No. 7 has been using the said land as his only passage so he filed an application on 17.7.1999 to writ-respondent No. 1 leasing out the said land to him. But by keeping the application of writ respondent No. 7 pending, the land of R.S. plot 1101 (part) including R.S. plot No.  1435 (part) was leased out to the writ-petitioner. On coming to know about the said lease writ-respondent No. 7 filed several applications to writ-respondent No.  1 for leasing out the said land of R.S. plot 1101 to him by cancelling the earlier allotment of the writ-petitioner. Considering the above facts, writ-respondent No. 1 informed the writ petitioner about the above mentioned irregularity of lease and after discussion with the writ petitioner cancelled his allotment and allotted 2.98 kathas of land of R.S. plot No. 1101 to writ-respondent No. 7 on 4.12.2004 (Annexure-K to the writ petition). On receipt of entire lease money writ-respondent No. 1 registered the lease deed, and handed over possession of the lease hold property to writ-respondent No. 7. Writ-respondent No. 7 has since been possessing the lease hold property as his passage from his other properties.
